name: favourites-grid-caps-at-four
description:
Rework, cap raised from 3 to 4. The favourites grid used to size its columns off a fixed repeat(3, ...), so it also showed 3 columns at the narrow default width where a tile has no room to be readable. It is now repeat(auto-fill, minmax(max(45px, calc((100% - 24px) / 4)), 1fr)): the /4 term caps the row at 4 columns however wide the sidebar gets, and the 45px floor puts the step from 3 to 4 columns under the 220 default, so the default shows four and only the 160px minimum shows two. The fixture stages 5 favourites and appState.sidebarWidth 520 - above kMaxSidebarWidth (500), so the first read also proves the out-of-range value clamps rather than reaching the page unclamped.

THE READS ARE LAYOUT, NOT A CAPTURE, for the same reason overview-widens-the-sidebar reads clientWidth instead of a frame: offsetTop/offsetLeft name the column count itself rather than a picture that a reviewer would still have to count tiles in. Grouping tiles by their offsetTop rather than assuming a fixed row height keeps the read honest if the tile height ever changes.

first-row-cols is the number of distinct offsetLeft values among tiles that share the smallest offsetTop - the columns actually occupied in the top row. row-count is the number of distinct offsetTop values across all 5 tiles. The scenario reads both at the fixture's clamped-wide width (500) and again after dragging the docked grip down to the 220 default, so the same 5 favourites prove the clamp and the /4 cap: 4 columns at both the clamped-wide width and the 220 default.

VACUITY GUARD: all 5 fixture favourites actually rendered as tiles, so the column reads below are counting something real

actions.expression: (() => { const els = [...document.querySelectorAll('.favgrid .fav')]; const minTop = Math.min(...els.map(e => e.offsetTop)); const lefts = new Set(els.filter(e => e.offsetTop === minTop).map(e => e.offsetLeft)); return lefts.size; })()
